$comment: VAPP-91: the host router (catalog/host.json ops): server messages in, ops out, in order. Inputs hand-written; `expected` filled by the generator from src/host/router.ts. A conformance runner creates ONE router per flow with `extensionIds`, installs `packages` (their install issues are `installIssues`), then routes every step's message and compares the ops. VAPP-122: `records` = validateRecord(packages[package].records[kind].schema, data) → issues; `acme.hours` declares two kinds, `acme.badrecords` every schema mistake. Keys of `records` and of every `properties` are written in sorted order: the Rust core iterates its maps sorted, so the issue order is the same on every platform. VAPP-161 (format version 2): `acme.v2` uses every new key validly (formatVersion, a records: binding, the records.* functions, the three tool transports, an empty extensions list); `acme.charts` declares an extension: not available under the default catalogs, installed by the VAPP-161 flow that registers it; `acme.v2broken` makes every tools / extensions / records-source mistake; `acme.future` is a newer format version; `acme.v1` is a version-1 package that stays valid. VAPP-180: `acme.exposes` declares `upstreams` and valid `exposes` (a records read and upsert, two action bindings, an upstream); `acme.badexposes` makes every format mistake of an exposed tool, a duplicate upstream included; `acme.exposeslist` has neither list a list.
